title: Duplicate PR's original resolved, the duplicate never did
author: off-by-one
description: Compares open pull requests against the repository's own PR set: a PR's body names itself 'duplicate of #N' (or 'dup of #N'), and #N has since merged or closed, but the duplicate itself was never closed alongside it. The PR-side twin of duplicate-issue-still-open -- GitHub gives this seam no auto-close mechanism at all -- a duplicate marker is pure prose, not a closing keyword -- so the gap has no trigger that could have fired and can persist indefinitely with nobody noticing.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the named original has been resolved (merged or closed) while the duplicate sits open, not flat. Under 24 hours since the original resolved scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- a human filing a duplicate PR may not have circled back within a day of the original landing). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal, a duplicate marker naming a PR number that already reads merged or closed. The 24h window matches duplicate-issue-still-open's own bar exactly (a clear, easily-verified resolution signal deserves a short grace window, not a long one) -- no stated reason to trust a PR-side resolution signal less than an issue-side one. A PR naming no duplicate marker, or naming an original that is still open, is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the identical discipline every recipe before this one holds.
